landmarks.name: Lake Ohrid
landmarks.writeup: One of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, known for its biodiversity and UNESCO World Heritage status.

landmarks.name: Skopje Fortress (Kale)
landmarks.writeup: Historic fortress overlooking the capital city, dating back to the 6th century.

landmarks.name: St. Jovan Bigorski Monastery
landmarks.writeup: An important Orthodox monastery renowned for its woodcarvings and religious significance.

landmarks.name: Stone Bridge
landmarks.writeup: Iconic Ottoman-era bridge connecting the old and new parts of Skopje.

landmarks.name: Mavrovo National Park
landmarks.writeup: A large national park known for its mountains, forests, and winter sports facilities.

cultural_events.name: Ohrid Summer Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Annual cultural festival featuring music, theater, and dance performances in the historic town of Ohrid.

cultural_events.name: Skopje Jazz Festival
cultural_events.writeup: International jazz festival attracting artists from around the world.

cultural_events.name: Vevchani Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: Traditional pre-Lenten carnival known for its colorful masks and costumes.

food_writeup: North Macedonian cuisine blends Mediterranean and Balkan influences, featuring dishes like tavne gravne (baked beans), ajvar (pepper spread), and various grilled meats.
brief_history: North Macedonia declared independence from Yugoslavia in 1991. It resolved a long-standing name dispute with Greece in 2019, adopting the name North Macedonia. The country has a rich history influenced by Roman, Byzantine, Ottoman, and Slavic cultures.

important_people.name: Kiro Gligorov (first President of independent Macedonia)

current_conflicts: No active armed conflicts; ongoing political and ethnic tensions occasionally arise between Macedonian and Albanian communities.
